solution.label: Class diagram of the photo collage redesign
solution.description: Photo and Split both implement the Tile interface, which declares draw(area, canvas) and photoCount(). Photo keeps a name. Split keeps a direction, offers add(tile: Tile), and holds any number of Tiles, so its tiles may be photos or other splits. ShareButton holds one Tile as its selection and offers press(), which returns the canvas.
solution.caption: A dashed arrow with a hollow triangle means a class implements an interface. The arrow with a hollow diamond means a Split holds any number of Tiles, which may be photos or other splits. The plain arrow means a ShareButton uses one Tile.

solution_caption.label: Class diagram with the Caption class added
solution_caption.description: As before, Photo and Split implement Tile, Split holds any number of Tiles, and ShareButton uses one Tile. A new class, Caption, keeps a text and also implements Tile, with draw(area, canvas) and photoCount(). No other class changed.
solution_caption.caption: Caption is one new class that implements Tile. Split and ShareButton are unchanged: a split holds Tiles, so it can hold captions too.

trace.label: Sequence of one press of Share on the story
trace.description: The Share button, button, calls draw(whole story, canvas) on story. story calls draw(left half, canvas) on beach, which draws itself, and then draw(right half, canvas) on right.
trace.caption: Lifelines are named like the variables in the main program. The trace shows the first two levels: right forwards to cat and to bottom the same way, which the canvas shows. Messages appear as the narration reaches them.
trace.source:
@startuml
participant button: ShareButton
participant story: Split
participant beach: Photo
participant right: Split
steps:
activate button
button -> story: draw(whole story, canvas)
activate story
story -> beach: draw(left half, canvas)
activate beach
deactivate beach
story -> right: draw(right half, canvas)
activate right
deactivate right
deactivate story
deactivate button

roles.label: Composite pattern role diagram
roles.description: A Client uses the Component interface, which declares operation(). Leaf and Composite both implement Component. Composite also declares add(child: Component) and holds any number of Components as its children.
roles.caption: This is the safe arrangement, with add only in Composite; the transparent one also declares add in Component. Composite both implements Component and holds Components, so composites can contain composites.

cards.title: Benefit: simple clients
cards.text: Clients treat one tile and a whole split the same way, with no type checks; wherever one tile fits, a whole split fits too.

cards.title: Benefit: new kinds fit in
cards.text: A new kind of tile is one new class that implements the shared interface; existing splits and clients work with it unchanged.

cards.title: Liability: overly general
cards.text: A split that may hold only some kinds, such as a photos-only strip, cannot use the type system to restrict add; it needs a check at runtime.

cards.title: Liability: safety or transparency
cards.text: Add only in the composite is checked early but visible to clients; add in the component is uniform, but leaves reject it at runtime.

cards.title: A good fit
cards.text: Items nest inside groups, groups inside groups, and clients should not care which one they hold.

cards.title: Simpler designs
cards.text: No nesting: a plain list, like a carousel post. Only one kind of leaf: one class with an optional list of children.

cards.title: Neighbors
cards.text: A frame around one tile adds drawing: a Decorator. View trees in Model-View-Controller and macro commands are composites.

cards.title: Context
cards.text: A part-whole hierarchy that nests, whose clients want to treat one object and a group alike.

cards.title: Problem
cards.text: Code that asks every item whether it is single or a group repeats its type checks, and silently misses new kinds.

cards.title: Solution
cards.text: A Component interface that Leaves implement directly and Composites implement by forwarding to their children.

cards.title: Consequences
cards.text: Simple clients and easy new kinds, at the cost of an overly general structure and a choice between safety and transparency.
